1.text:
Under the usual approval–ballot formulation a group $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff

* $|S|\ge \ell n/k $ and
* $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell $,

and $W$ satisfies EJR iff for every $\ell$-cohesive $S$ every $i\in S$
has $|A_{i}\cap W|\ge\ell$.  Here $n=10,\;k=5,\;n/k=2$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3\cdot2$ and $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|\bigcap|=3$.  Hence $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive.  For $i\in S_{X}$ we have
$|A_{i}\cap W|\ge3$ for every $i$.  In particular for $8,9,10$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=|\,\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cap W\,|+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}\ge3$,
for $2$ $|\, \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cap W\,|+{\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}\ge3$, etc.
The only way to give the six voters three representatives with $|W|=5$
is to take the three common $x$’s in $W$.  With $a=|\,\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cap
W\,|$ we need $a\ge3$ and $a\le3$, i.e. $a=3$ and
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\subseteq W$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2\cdot2$ and $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|\bigcap|=3$.  Hence $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive.  For $i=4,5$
$|A_{i}\cap W|=|\,\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}\cap W\,|+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}\ge2$
and for $i=6,7$ 
$|A_{i}\cap W|=|\,\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}\cap W\,|+{\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}\ge2$.
With the three $x$’s already used the only way to give $4,5,6,7$ two
representatives each in a $5$-set is to put $b\ge2$ members of
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ in $W$ and no further outside candidate.
$|W|=5$ then forces $b=2$ and $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{i},y_{j}\}$ with
$\{y_{i},y_{j}\}\subset\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

In particular

$|A_{1}\cap W|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cap W|
+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}=3+0+0=3$

for every EJR committee.  Up to the choice of the two $y$’s the
EJR committee is essentially unique, so voter 1 is represented by three
and only three of his five approved candidates.

*If EJR is taken in the “existential’’ form
$|S|\ge\ell n/k,\;|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell\Rightarrow\exists i\in S:
|A_{i}\cap W|\ge\ell$, the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ only forces the existence
of a voter in $S_{X}$ with three representatives and the $2$-cohesive
$S_{Y}$ only forces the existence of a $Y$-voter with two representatives.
The cheapest $Y$-realisation is two $Y$-candidates, leaving at most three
places for $A_{1}$.  The cheapest $X$-realisation is $a=2$ $x$’s together
with $y_{2}$ – or $y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ – giving $|A_{1}\cap W|=2$, and the
most $A_{1}$-friendly realisation is $a=3$ $x$’s together with two $Y$
candidates, giving $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$.  Hence in the existential
formulation $2\le|A_{1}\cap W|\le3$, i.e. the usual min $2$ max $3$
range. ∎

For $k=5$, $n=10$ EJR is $\lvert S\rvert\ge 2\ell\Rightarrow \max_{i\in S}
|C\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.
Put
$a=|C\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|C\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2},z_{3}\in\{0,1\}$ in $C$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{1}&=a+y_{1}+z_{3} &&{\rm voter\;1}\\
a_{2}&=a+y_{2} &&{\rm voter\;2}\\
a_{3}&=a+y_{3} &&{\rm voter\;3}\\
a_{8-10}&=a+z_{1} &&{\rm voters\;8,9,10}\\
a_{4,5}&=b+z_{1}&&{\rm voters\;4,5}\\
a_{6,7}&=b+z_{2}&&{\rm voters\;6,7}
\end{aligned}
$$

$\ell=3$ needs a voter with $\ge3$ approvals in every $6$-set, hence at most five
voters can have $\le2$ approvals and at most three voters can have $\le1$
approval.

$a=0$ gives $a_{2},a_{3},a_{8-10}\le1$ and $a_{1}\le2$, i.e. $\ge5$ voters with
$\le1$, impossible.  Hence $a\ge1$.

$c(v_{1})=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$ is the number of approved members for voter 1.
$c=1$ forces, up to symmetry, $a=1,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0$.
Then $a_{1}=1$, $a_{2}=1+y_{2}$, $a_{3}=1+y_{3}$, $a_{8-10}=1+z_{1}$.
To keep $\le3$ voters with $\le1$ we need $z_{1}=1$, $y_{2}=y_{3}=1$.
With $a=1,z_{1}=1$, $y_{2}+y_{3}=2$ we have
$b+y_{2}+y_{3}+z_{1}+z_{2}=4$.  The only way to obtain a voter with $\ge3$
is $b+z_{1}\ge3$ or $b+z_{2}\ge3$, i.e. $b\ge2$ and $z_{1}=1$.  Then
$\{v_{1},v_{2},v_{3},v_{8},v_{9},v_{10}\}$ is a $6$-set whose members all have
$\le2$ approvals, contradicting $\ell=3$.  Hence $c\ge2$.

$c=2$ is attainable.  e.g. 
$C=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;b=2,\;z_{1}=1$.
$$
a_{1}=2,\;a_{2}=a_{3}=2,\;a_{8-10}=3,\;a_{4,5}=3,\;a_{6,7}=2 .
$$
The $5$ voters with $\ge3$ approvals are $v_{4},v_{5},v_{8},v_{9},v_{10}$;
any $6$-set meets them, every $4$-set meets a voter with $\ge2$, and every
$2$-set meets a voter with $\ge1$.  Hence the committee is EJR and
$|C\cap A_{1}|=2$.

The upper bound follows from the $B$-cluster.  Voters $4$–$7$ need a voter
with $\ge2$ approvals, so $b+z_{1}\ge2$ or $b+z_{2}\ge2$.  With $c=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$
seats, $5-c$ seats remain for the $B$-side.  If $c\ge4$ at most one seat is
left for $B$, whence $b+z_{1}\le1$ and $b+z_{2}\le1$, contradicting the
$\ell=2$ condition for $\{4,5,6,7\}$.  Hence $c\le3$.

$c=3$ is attainable, e.g.
$C=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;b=2$.
Then $a_{1}=a_{2}=a_{3}=a_{8-10}=3$ and $a_{4,5}=a_{6,7}=2$, which is EJR and
$|C\cap A_{1}|=3$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can contain $2$ or $3$ of voter 1’s approved
candidates, and both extremes are attainable. ∎

3.text:
Under the usual approval version

* $n/k=2$ .
* for $\ell$ let $H_{\ell}=\{i:|W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell\}$.
$ |S|\ge\ell n/k$ must meet $H_{\ell}$, hence
$|H_{\ell}|\ge n-\ell n/k+1$.

Hence

* $|H_{2}|\ge 10-4+1=7$,
* $|H_{3}|\ge 10-6+1=5$,
* $|H_{4}|\ge 10-8+1=3$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.

* $V_{8},V_{9},V_{10}$ have $A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$,
* $V_{4},V_{5}$ have $A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
* $V_{6},V_{7}$ have $A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.

A $4$-approval for an $X$ voter needs $a\ge3$ and the extra
candidate $z_{1},y_{2}$ or $y_{3}$. A $4$-approval for a $Y$ voter needs
the whole $4$-set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ or $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
A mixed $H_{4}$ is impossible with five seats, so $H_{4}$ is either
$X$-only or $Y$-only.

$Y$-only $H_{4}$ forces $W=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$|H_{3}|=4<5$.  Hence $H_{4}$ must be $X$-only.  The cheapest
$X$-only $H_{4}$ is $V_{8},V_{9},V_{10}$ with

\[
W\supset\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\},
\]

so $a\ge3$ and $z_{1}\in W$.  With $a=3$ we have

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a=3
\]

if the fifth seat is taken outside $A_{1}$.  E.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

$|W\cap A_{i}|$ :

$1,2,3:3$, $4,5:2$, $6,7:1$, $8,9,10:4$,

so $|H_{4}|=3$, $|H_{3}|=6\ge5$, $|H_{2}|=8\ge7$, i.e. EJR holds.

$a\ge3$ is necessary for an $X$ $4$-approval, whence
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  With $t=|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ we have at most one
non-$A_{1}$ seat, so no $Y$ voter can reach $2$ approvals and

$|H_{2}|\le |\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}|=6<7$,

so $t\ge4$ is impossible.  Hence $t=3$ is both necessary and
sufficient.

Min $= $ Max $=3$.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: E. min 3, max 3

2.text:
The individual EJR condition is

$|S|\ge 2\ell\Longrightarrow\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell $

i.e. at most $ \ell n/k-1$ voters can be $<\ell$–represented.  
Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
$z_{1},z_{2}\in\{0,1\}$,
$o=p_{1}+q_{2}+q_{3}$ with $p_{1}=[y_{1}]+[z_{3}]$, $q_{2}=[y_{2}]$, 
$q_{3}=[y_{3}]$,

$a+y+z_{1}+z_{2}+o=5$.  Then

* $A_{8,9,10}: a+z_{1}$,
* $A_{1}:a+p_{1}$,
* $A_{2}:a+q_{2}$,
* $A_{3}:a+q_{3}$,
* $A_{4,5}:y+z_{1}$,
* $A_{6,7}:y+z_{2}$.

For $\ell=3$, $\ell n/k=6$, so at most five voters may have
$|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$.  
For $\ell=2$, $\ell n/k=4$, so at most three voters may have
$|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$.
The three $A$ voters $8,9,10$ and the two $B$ voters $4,5$ force
$a+z_{1}\ge2$ and $y+z_{1}\ge2$ etc.

The feasible region is obtained with $z_{1}=1$, $z_{2}=0$.  
Then $a+y+o=4$ and $y\ge1$.  The $\ell=3$ condition gives
$a+z_{1}\ge3$ or $y+z_{1}\ge3$ and the $6$–voter worst case is

$\#\{|W\cap A_{i}|\le2\}\le5$.

The smallest possible overlap with voter 1 is
$O=a+p_{1}$.  With $z_{1}=1$, $y=2$, $a=2$, $o=0$ we obtain

$W=\{x_{i},x_{j},y_{k},y_{\ell},z_{1}\}$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=y+z_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=y=2$, etc.,
so $\#\{|W\cap A_{i}|\le2\}=5$ and $\#\{|W\cap A_{i}|\le1\}=0$.
Hence $O_{\min}=2$ is attainable and $O\ge2$ is necessary.

The largest possible overlap is obtained with $a$ maximal.  With
$a=3$, $y=1$, $z_{1}=1$, $o=0$

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$

gives

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=4$, $|W\cap A_{1,2,3}|=3$, 
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$,

so $\#\{|W\cap A_{i}|\le2\}=4<6$ and $\#\{|W\cap A_{i}|\le1\}=2<4$,
i.e. the committee is individually EJR and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=3$.  $O=4$ would need $a+p_{1}\ge4$, which forces
$4$ voters to have $|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$, contradicting the $\ell=2$
condition.  Hence $O_{\max}=3$.

Hence an EJR committee can contain $2$ and can contain $3$ of the
candidates approved by voter 1, and both bounds are attainable.
This is option H : min 2, max 3.

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1},z_{2},y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{3}\in\{0,1\}$,
$a+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+z_{3}=5$.

$|W\cap A_{i}|$ is
$v_{1}=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$,
$v_{2}=a+y_{2}$, $v_{3}=a+y_{3}$,
$v_{8-10}=a+z_{1}$,

$\ell=3$ cohesive sets: $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, 
$\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|\bigcap|=3$.
Hence $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$, i.e.
$a+\max\{y_{1}+z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$.

$\ell=2$ cohesive sets: $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$,

Hence $\max\{b+z_{1},b+z_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.

needs $a+\max\{y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$.  $a\ge2$ is necessary, and

3.text:
The  $n/k=2$  so that a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.  With the usual existential
formulation of EJR

$|S|\ge 2\ell,\;|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell\Longrightarrow
\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell $

put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1},z_{2}\in\{0,1\}$, $y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.

Then

\begin{align*}
a_{1}&=a+y_{1}+z_{3}, & a_{2}&=a+y_{2}, & a_{3}&=a+y_{3},\\
a_{8,9,10}&=a+z_{1}, &
a_{4,5}&=b+z_{1}, &
a_{6,7}&=b+z_{2},
\end{align*}
$a+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+z_{3}=5$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is $3$-cohesive and
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is $2$-cohesive.  With $H_{\ell}
=\{i:|W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell\}$ EJR is $|H_{\ell}|\ge n-2\ell+1$, i.e.
$|H_{2}|\ge7$, $|H_{3}|\ge5$.

The cheapest way to meet $S_{Y}$ is $b+z_{1}\ge2$ and $b+z_{2}\ge2$.
The cheapest way to meet $S_{X}$ is to have at least one $X$-voter
with three approvals.  With $z_{1}=1$ we can take $a=2$, $b=2$ and
$o=y_{2}+y_{3}=0$, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;b=2,\;z_{1}=1$.  Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\;|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{3}|=2,\;
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3,\;
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=3,\;
|W\cap A_{6,7}|=2,$

so $|H_{3}|=3$, $|H_{2}|=8\ge7$ and every $6$-set and every $4$-set
meets $H_{3}$ resp. $H_{2}$.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ is attainable
and $2$ is the obvious lower bound, $a=0$ would give five voters with
$\le1$ approval.

If $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}\ge4$ then at most one seat is left
outside $A_{1}$.  Then $b+z_{1}\le1$ and $b+z_{2}\le1$ so no $Y$-voter
can reach two approvals and $|H_{2}|\le|\,\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\,|=6<7$,
contradicting EJR.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

The upper bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;b=2$.  Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{3}|=|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so $|H_{3}|=6\ge5$, $|H_{2}|=10\ge7$, i.e. the committee is
EJR-existential and $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

Thus in the usual existential formulation EJR allows

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the minimum $2$ being realised by e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$
and the maximum $3$ by e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
This is the min $2$, max $3$ range, option H.  The universal
“every $i\in S$’’ reading of EJR is the strong version and gives the
unique value $3$, option E. ∎

Public response:

$n=10,\;k=5,\;n/k=2$.  Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;z_{2}={\bf 1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,

$a+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+o=5$ with $o$ the number of seats taken outside
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

Then

* $A_{8,9,10}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$ : $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$,
* $A_{1}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ : $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p_{1}$,
  $p_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $A_{2}=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;A_{3}=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,
* $A_{4,5}=b+z_{1},\;A_{6,7}=b+z_{2}$.

The $6$ voter $X$-cluster $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, 
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$ and $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
is $3$-cohesive and the $4$ voter $Y$-cluster
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$ and 
$\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, is $2$-cohesive.

For $\ell=3$, $\ell n/k=6$.  An EJR committee in the usual
existential form

$|S|\ge\ell n/k,\;|\bigcap_{S}A_{i}|\ge\ell\Longrightarrow
\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$

must have at most $5$ voters with $|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and at most $3$
voters with $|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$.  The three $X$ voters $8,9,10$ force
$a+z_{1}\ge3$ on any realisation which meets the $3$-cohesive set.
The cheapest existential realisation is therefore

$z_{1}=1,\;z_{2}=0,\;a=2,\;b=2,\;o=0$,

e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;b=2,\;z_{1}=1$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=2$, 
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+z_{1}=3$, 
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$,

$\#\{i:|W\cap A_{i}|\le2\}=5$, $\#\{i:|W\cap A_{i}|\le1\}=0$,
so the $\ell=3$ and $\ell=2$ existential conditions are met.
Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ is attainable and $ |W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ is
necessary; $a=1$ would give five voters with $|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$.

The $A_{1}$-friendly extremum is obtained with $a$ maximal under the
$Y$-constraint $b+z_{1}\ge2$ or $b+z_{2}\ge2$. With $z_{1}=1$ the
maximal $a$ compatible with the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is $a=3$,
$b=1$, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a=3$, 
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}=4$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+z_{1}=2$, 
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=1$,

$\#\{i:|W\cap A_{i}|\le2\}=4<6$, $\#\{i:|W\cap A_{i}|\le1\}=2<4$.
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would need $a+p_{1}\ge4$ and hence at most one seat
left for the $Y$-side, which makes $b+z_{1}\le1$ and $b+z_{2}\le1$ and
violates the $\ell=2$ existential condition on $S_{Y}$.

Hence in the conventional existential definition of EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$

and both bounds are attainable, e.g. $2$ with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$. This is the usual
min $2$ max $3$ range, option H.

Remark.  With the stronger “for-all’’ reading
$|S|\ge\ell n/k,\;|\bigcap_{S}A_{i}|\ge\ell\Rightarrow
\forall i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$,
the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ forces $a+z_{1}\ge3$ for the three voters
$8,9,10$ and hence $a=3$, $z_{1}=1$, $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\subseteq W$.
Together with the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ this forces
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{i},y_{j}\}$, $y_{i},y_{j}\subset\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
and $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ for every such committee, i.e. the
for-all min $=$ max $=3$ essentially unique EJR committee of option E.
∎

4.text:
The $5$-set $W$ can be described by

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$d_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},d_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},d_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W},
e={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,

$a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{1}+d_{2}+d_{3}+e=5$.
Put

$\begin{array}{lll}
v_{1}=a+d_{1}+e, & v_{2}=a+d_{2}, & v_{3}=a+d_{3},\\
v_{8,9,10}=a+c_{1}, & v_{4,5}=b+c_{1}, & v_{6,7}=b+c_{2}.
\end{array}$

$|S_{X}|=6,\;\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ gives the $\ell=3$
existential condition

$\max\{a+d_{1}+e,a+d_{2},a+d_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3 , \tag{1}$

and $|S_{Y}|=4,\;\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ gives the $\ell=2$
existential condition

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2 .\tag{2}$

$C_{3}$ forces $a\ge2$.  With $d_{1}=e=0$ put $v_{1}=a$.  Then
$a\ge2$ and (1) is $a+\max\{d_{2},d_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$.
With $a=2$ we can take $c_{1}=1,\;b=1,\;d_{2}=1$, the other
indicators $0$.  Then

$W=\{x_{i},x_{j},y_{k},y_{\ell},z_{1}\},\qquad a=2,b=2,c_{1}=1$,

$v_{1}=2,\;v_{2}=v_{3}=2,\;v_{8,9,10}=3,\;v_{4,5}=3,\;v_{6,7}=2$,

so $\max_{S_{X}}v_{i}=3$ and $\max_{S_{Y}}v_{i}=2$.  Hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.  $v_{1}=1$ would need
$a\le1$ and would make the left hand side of (1) $\le2$, so $v_{1}\ge2$.

For the upper bound, $v_{1}=a+d_{1}+e\le3$ unless $a\ge2$ and
$d_{1}+e\ge2$.  If $a=3$ then $b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{1}+d_{2}+d_{3}+e=2$ and
(2) forces $d_{1}=e=0$, $b\ge1$, $c_{1}\ge1$, whence $v_{1}=3$.
If $a=2$ and $d_{1}+e=2$ then $b+c_{1}+c_{2}+d_{2}+d_{3}=1$, so
$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  Hence $d_{1}+e\le1$
when $a=2$ and $v_{1}=a+d_{1}+e\le3$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},\qquad a=3,b=2$,

$v_{1}=v_{2}=v_{3}=v_{8,9,10}=3$, $v_{4,5}=v_{6,7}=2$,

which is EJR and $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

Hence under the existential EJR

$$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,$$

and both $2$ and $3$ are attainable, e.g. $2$ with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and $3$ with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  This is the min-2 max-3 range,
option H.  With the universal “every $i\in S$’’ reading the $3$-cohesive
$S_{X}$ forces $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\subseteq W$ and the $Y$-block
forces $b\ge2$, giving the essentially unique committee with
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ for every EJR committee.

The $n/k=2$ and the only $\ell$--cohesive groups that can occur are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $3$--cohesive;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $2$--cohesive.

Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\qquad b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$

and $z_{1},z_{2},y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.  With
$a+b+z_{1}+z_{2}+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+z_{3}=5$

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{1}&=a+y_{1}+z_{3},& a_{2}&=a+y_{2},& a_{3}&=a+y_{3},\\
a_{8-10}&=a+z_{1},&a_{4,5}&=b+z_{1},&a_{6,7}&=b+z_{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

EJR for the two cohesive groups is

* $\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,  the
$3$--cohesive $S_{X}$,
* $\max\{b+z_{1},b+z_{2}\}\ge 2$, the $2$--cohesive $S_{Y}$.

Let $c=|A_{1}\cap W|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.

$a\ge1$ is forced, otherwise the first max is $\le2$.  $c=1$ would give
$a=1,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0$ and then $\max\{a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\le2$,
so $c\ge2$.  

$c=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;b=2,\;z_{1}=1$.
Then
$a_{1}=2,\;a_{2}=a_{3}=2,\;a_{8-10}=3,\;a_{4,5}=3,\;a_{6,7}=2$,
$\max_{S_{X}}=3$ and $\max_{S_{Y}}=3$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are both
represented and $W$ is EJR.  Hence $c_{\min}=2$.

If $c\ge4$ then $5-c\le1$ seats are left for the $Y$--cluster, whence
$b+z_{1}\le1$ and $b+z_{2}\le1$, contradicting $\max\{b+z_{1},b+z_{2}\}\ge2$.
Hence $c\le3$, and $c=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;b=2$,
$a_{1}=a_{2}=a_{3}=a_{8-10}=3$, $a_{4,5}=a_{6,7}=2$,

so $\max_{S_{X}}=3$, $\max_{S_{Y}}=2$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$.

Hence with the existential EJR

$2\le|A_{1}\cap W|\le3$,

the lower bound $2$ and the upper bound $3$ are both attainable.  This is
the usual $ \min 2,\max 3$ range, option H.

The per-voter “strong’’ reading $\forall i\in S\;|A_{i}\cap W|\ge\ell$
forces $a=3$, $z_{1}=z_{2}=0$, $b=2$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|=3$ for every
EJR committee, i.e. the $ \min 3,\max 3$ case.
